title: A drive says it is failing
why: A drive that fails its own health test can stop working without warning, and anything on it may be lost.
fix_summary: Copy your files to another drive now. Nothing is changed on the failing drive.
manual: Back up your files first. Then replace the drive. Do not run repairs on it until your files are safe.

title: A drive has damaged spots
why: Damaged spots on a drive usually keep spreading. The files stored there may become unreadable.
fix_summary: Copy your files to another drive now. Nothing is changed on the drive.
manual: Back up your files, then plan to replace the drive.

title: A fast drive (NVMe) reports a critical warning
why: The drive is telling the computer that it may stop working or become read-only very soon.
fix_summary: Copy your files to another drive now. Nothing is changed on the drive.
manual: Back up your files and replace the drive.

title: A drive is wearing out
why: Drives have a limited number of writes. Near the end they get slow and then stop accepting data.
fix_summary: Make sure your backups are up to date, then plan a replacement.
manual: Check your backups are recent and plan to replace the drive in the next few months.

title: A drive is running too hot
why: Heat shortens the life of a drive and can cause errors.
fix_summary: Nothing to change in software. Improve air flow.
manual: Clean the vents and fans, and make sure nothing blocks the air flow.

title: The cable to a drive is dropping data
why: A loose or worn cable makes the drive slow or error-prone, even if the drive itself is fine.
fix_summary: Nothing to change in software.
manual: Switch off, unplug the power, re-seat or replace the drive's data cable. Back up first if you can.

title: The drive's own test found a reading problem
why: When a drive fails its own test it can no longer be trusted with your files.
fix_summary: Copy your files to another drive now.
manual: Back up now and replace the drive.

detector: health:storage:*-io=FAIL || cmd:klog~Buffer I/O error|blk_update_request: I/O error|ata[0-9.]+: .*failed command#3
title: The computer had trouble reading or writing a drive
why: Read or write errors are an early sign of a failing drive, a bad cable or a failing USB port.
fix_summary: Copy your files to another drive now, then check the cable.
manual: Back up your files. Re-seat the cable and try again; if errors continue the drive is failing.

title: A fast drive (NVMe) keeps timing out
why: The drive stops answering for a moment, which can freeze the computer for a few seconds.
fix_summary: Nothing automatic. Updating the computer's firmware often fixes it.
manual: Install firmware updates (Software > Updates) and keep a backup.

title: A drive is very slow
why: A slow drive makes everything feel slow, and slow reading can be an early sign of trouble.
fix_summary: Nothing to change automatically.
manual: Try another USB port or cable; if it is an old hard drive, back it up and consider an SSD.

title: The disk's file records have errors (ext4)
why: Damaged file records can make files unreadable and, if ignored, get worse.
fix_summary: Open the disk check helper. It checks and repairs the disk while it is not in use.
backup_first: A backup of important files is suggested first.
undo: The helper keeps a log of what it changed.
manual: Start from the rescue stick and choose Check and repair a disk.

title: The disk's file records have errors (Btrfs)
why: Btrfs found data that does not match its checksum. That can mean a failing drive or damaged files.
fix_summary: Run a full read-through check (scrub). It repairs what it can from spare copies and lists what it cannot.
backup_first: A backup of important files is suggested first.
undo: Not applicable: a scrub only reads and repairs.
manual: Run: sudo btrfs scrub start -B / and read the result.

title: The disk's file records have errors (XFS)
why: Damaged records can make files unreadable.
fix_summary: Open the disk check helper, which runs the right repair while the disk is not in use.
backup_first: A backup of important files is suggested first.
manual: Start from the rescue stick and choose Check and repair a disk.

title: A USB drive or card (exFAT) has errors
why: The drive was probably removed without ejecting. Files may be missing or damaged.
fix_summary: Open the disk check helper to check the drive.
manual: Plug it into the computer and choose Check and repair a disk.

title: The last start-up could not finish checking a drive
why: The automatic disk check failed, so the drive may have unfixed errors.
fix_summary: Open the disk check helper to run the check by hand.
backup_first: A backup of important files is suggested first.
manual: Start from the rescue stick and choose Check and repair a disk.

title: The main disk has gone read-only
why: Linux makes a disk read-only when it finds errors, to protect your files. You cannot save anything until it is fixed.
fix_summary: Open the disk check helper, then restart.
backup_first: Copy files you need to another drive first.
manual: Restart. If it stays read-only, start from the rescue stick and run Check and repair a disk.

title: The main disk is almost full
what: The main disk is {detail}% full. Programs may fail to save, update or start.
why: A full disk causes strange errors, slow updates and failed logins.
fix_summary: Delete only safe leftovers: old download lists, old logs, unused app parts and the recycle bin of old updates. Your files are not touched.
undo: Not applicable: only temporary files are removed.
manual: Empty the bin, remove old downloads, and uninstall apps you do not use.

title: The main disk has too many small files
what: The main disk has used {detail}% of the number of files it can hold, even if there is free space.
why: When the limit is reached, nothing new can be saved.
fix_summary: Nothing is deleted automatically, because the files could be yours.
manual: Find the folder with the most files: sudo du --inodes -x / | sort -n | tail. Often a mail or cache folder.

title: The disk for your files is almost full
what: The disk that holds your files (/home) is {detail}% full.
why: You may soon be unable to save documents or photos.
fix_summary: Nothing is deleted automatically, because the files are yours.
manual: Look for big folders (Downloads, Videos, old backups) in a disk usage tool, and move or delete what you do not need.

title: The disk may run out of space even though it shows free space
what: Btrfs has less than 1 GB of unused room to hand out, which can cause "no space left" errors even with free space.
why: Over time the disk's space gets split into chunks that cannot be reused.
fix_summary: Tidy the disk's chunks (a "balance") so free space becomes usable again. Your files are not changed.
manual: Run: sudo btrfs balance start -dusage=10 -musage=5 /

title: The disk has not been checked for hidden damage in months
what: The last full read-through check (scrub) was {detail} days ago, or never.
why: A scrub finds quiet damage early, while you can still fix it.
fix_summary: Run a read-through check of the disk. It runs in the background and only reads.
manual: Run: sudo btrfs scrub start /

title: There is no spare memory space
what: The computer has no compressed memory (zram) or swap space, and not much real memory.
why: When memory runs out, programs get closed or the computer freezes.
fix_summary: Turn on compressed memory (zram). It uses a little real memory to hold more.
undo: Run: sudo systemctl stop systemd-zram-setup@zram0 and remove the setting file.
manual: Install zram-generator and restart.

title: The computer is short of memory
what: The spare memory space is {detail}% used, so the computer is probably running slowly.
why: When memory and spare space are both full, programs freeze or are closed.
fix_summary: Nothing changes automatically; closing programs helps.
manual: Close browser tabs and programs you are not using, then restart the computer.

title: The weekly tidy-up for the SSD is off
what: The computer has an SSD but the weekly tidy-up (TRIM) that keeps it fast is not switched on.
why: Without it the SSD slowly gets slower and wears more.
fix_summary: Switch on the weekly SSD tidy-up. It runs quietly in the background.
manual: Run: sudo systemctl enable --now fstrim.timer

title: A USB stick or card is giving errors
why: USB sticks and SD cards wear out, and a damaged one loses files without warning.
fix_summary: Copy what you can off it now, then stop using it.
manual: Copy the files off it right away and replace it. Do not use it for important files again.

title: A mirrored set of drives has lost a drive
what: The set of drives that protect each other (RAID) is running with a missing or failed drive.
why: It still works, but one more failure would lose data.
fix_summary: Back up now, then replace the failed drive.
manual: Back up, replace the failed drive and re-add it with mdadm.
